paite: Huan, Joseph in apa mai a, sia, a kaha, a tawptawpa.
english: Joseph fell on his father’s face, wept on him, and kissed him.

paite: Huan, Josephin a sikha damdawi siamte a pa luang muat theiloua bawl dingin thu a piaa: huchiin damdawi siamten Isreal luang muat theilouin a bawlta uhi.
english: Joseph commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father; and the physicians embalmed Israel.

paite: A luang bawlnain ni sawm li a zang ua, muat theiloua bawlnain ni huchizah ala nak ahi: huan, ni sawm sagih suang teng Aiguptaten amah a kah uhi.
english: Forty days were fulfilled for him, for that is how many the days it takes to embalm. The Egyptians wept for him for seventy days.

paite: Huan, amah a kah nite uh a bei nugin Josephin Pharo inkuante a houpiha, Hehpihtakin Pharo bila jak dingin, Ka pan, Ngaiin, si ding ka hita,
english: When the days of weeping for him were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, please speak in the ears of Pharaoh, saying,

paite: Kanan gam a ka han ka tohsa ah, hiailai ngeiah na honvui ding ahi, chiin, a honkichiamsaka, Huchiin, hehpihtakin ka pa hon vaposak inla, huan, ka hong pai nawn mai ding, a chi hi, chiin, gen un, a chi a.
english: ‘My father made me swear, saying, “Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my grave which I have dug for myself in the land of Canaan.” Now therefore, please let me go up and bury my father, and I will come again.’”

paite: Huchiin, Pharoin, A honkichiamsak bangin na pa vapo tou ve, a chi a.
english: Pharaoh said, “Go up, and bury your father, just like he made you swear.”

paite: Huchiin, Joseph bel a pa vui dingin a vahoh toua: huan, Pharo sikha tengteng, a innkuan laka upate leh Aigupta gam upa tengteng leh,
english: Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, all the elders of the land of Egypt,

paite: Joseph inkuanpihte tengteng leh, a unaute leh, a pa inkuanpihte, a kiangah a vahoh tou a: a tanu neu chikchikte uleh, a belam honte uleh a bawng honte kia uh Gosen gamah a nusia ua.
english: all the house of Joseph, his brothers, and his father’s house. Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

paite: Huan, a kiang uah kangtalaite. Sakol tungtuang mite toh, a hih ua; huchiin pawl lianpi ahi uh.
english: There went up with him both chariots and horsemen. It was a very great company.

paite: Huan Jordan lui gala Atadia phual a tuang ua, huailaiah nakpitakin a kah ua: ni sagih a pa sunna a bawl hi.
english: They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan, and there they lamented with a very great and severe lamentation. He mourned for his father seven days.

paite: Huan, hiai gama a mi Kananten, Atada phual a a mi sun uh a muh un, Hiai Aiguptate misi sunna thupital ahi, a chi ua: huaijiakin huai mun minin Abel-Mozraim a sa ua, huai Jordan lui gala om ahi.
english: When the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, “This is a grievous mourning by the Egyptians.” Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim, which is beyond the Jordan.

paite: Huan, a tapaten a thupiak bang jelin a hihsak ua:
english: His sons did to him just as he commanded them,

paite: A tapten Kanan gamah a jawng lut ua, Abrahamin, kivuina mun gou dinga, Hit mi Ephron akipana a lou toh a lei Mamre maa Makpel lou a kokhuk ah a vuita uhi.
english: for his sons carried him into the land of Canaan, and buried him in the cave of the field of Machpelah, which Abraham bought with the field, for a possession of a burial site, from Ephron the Hittite, before Mamre.

paite: Huan, Joseph bel, a pa a vui khitin, amah leh, a unaute leh, apa vui ding a kianga hohtoute tengteng toh, Aigupta gamah a pai nawnta uhi.
english: Joseph returned into Egypt—he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

paite: Huan, Joseph unauten a pa uh si a ngaihtuah un, Josephin hon mudah dinga, a tunga I thil hihkelh tengteng uh phu i tunguah kim sipsipin a honla kha ding e aw, a chi ua.
english: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said, “It may be that Joseph will hate us, and will fully pay us back for all of the evil which we did to him.”

paite: Huchiin, Joseph kiangah hilh dingin thu a khak ua, Na pan a sih main hichiin thu a pia,
english: They sent a message to Joseph, saying, “Your father commanded before he died, saying,

paite: Hichiin Joseph kiangah, hehpihtakin na unaute tatlekna leh a gilouhna uh ngaidamin, na tungah thil a hih leh a hihkhial na uh, chiin, na gen ding uh, a chi, chiin: huchiin hehpihtakin na pa Pathian sikhate tatlekna ngaidamin, a chi ua. Huan, a kianga a gentak un Joseph a kapta hi.
english: ‘You shall tell Joseph, “Now please forgive the disobedience of your brothers, and their sin, because they did evil to you.”’ Now, please forgive the disobedience of the servants of the God of your father.” Joseph wept when they spoke to him.

paite: Huan, a unaute leng a vahoh ua, a maah a khupboh chiat ua; huan, Ngaiin, na sikhate ka hi uhi, a chi ua.
english: His brothers also went and fell down before his face; and they said, “Behold, we are your servants.”

paite: Huan, Josephin, a kiang uah, Lau kei un: Pathian sika om ka hi hia?
english: Joseph said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for am I in the place of God?

paite: Nou jaw ka tungah thil gilou hih lungsimin na pu ua; himahleh Pathianin tuni bangin, mi tampi hing leh dama humbitna dinga, thil hoih a suahsak a lungsim put ahi jaw ngala.
english: As for you, you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save many people alive.

paite: Hichiin lau kei un: noute leh na ta na nau chikchikte ka hon vak jel ding, a chi a. Huchiin, a lungmuana, kam siam takin a houpih chiat hi.
english: Now therefore don’t be afraid. I will nourish you and your little ones.” He comforted them, and spoke kindly to them.

paite: Huan, Joseph bel, amah leh apa inkuanpihte toh, Aigupta gamah a om ua: Joseph kum ja leh kum sawm a dam hi.
english: Joseph lived in Egypt, he, and his father’s house. Joseph lived one hundred ten years.

paite: Josephin Ephraim ta, tusawn thum chiang a mu a: Manassi tapa Makir tate leng Joseph phei tungah a piang ua.
english: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.

paite: Huan, Josephin a unaute kiangah, si ding ka hita hi: himahleh Pathianin a hongveh ngeingei ding hi, hiai gam akipanin a hongpi khiain. Abraham te, Isaak te, Jakob te kianga kichiama piak achiam gamah a honpi tou ding, a chi a.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am dying, but God will surely visit you, and bring you up out of this land to the land which he swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.”

paite: Huan, Josephin Isreal suante a kichiam saka, Pathian in a hongveh ngeingei dinga, ka guhte hiai akipanin na jawng tou ding uh ahi, a chi a.Huchiin, Joseph bel, kum ja leh kum sawm a upa a hihin, a si a: huan, a luang muat theilouin a bawl ua, Aigupta gamah kuang ah a koih uh.
english: Joseph took an oath of the children of Israel, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones from here.”

paite: Huchiin, Joseph bel, kum ja leh kum sawm a upa a hihin, a si a: huan, a luang muat theilouin a bawl ua, Aigupta gamah kuang ah a koih uh.
english: So Joseph died, being one hundred ten years old, and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.
